title: OpenAI will test visual ads inside ChatGPT image generation this month
subtitle: Free and Go tiers will see product-inspiration ads during image generation; Plus, Pro, Business, and Enterprise subscribers remain ad-free.
author: AESOP AI Engine
body: OpenAI confirmed on October 5 that it will begin testing a visual ad format inside ChatGPT image generation later this month, with an initial group of US advertisers. The format shows product-inspiration imagery alongside — but visually separated from — the image a user is generating, with labels marking the content as advertising. OpenAI says ads will not influence ChatGPT's text answers. The surface is large: ChatGPT reaches roughly 1.2 billion people weekly across tiers, and the ad-eligible population is the Free and $8/month Go cohort. Plus, Pro, Business, and Enterprise subscribers remain ad-free.

The announcement is paired with concrete measurement plumbing. OpenAI is running brand-suitability pilots with DoubleVerify and Integral Ad Science, and has wired conversion tracking through Hightouch, Tealium, and LiveRamp with attribution via AppsFlyer, Adjust, and Branch. That stack is not an experimental widget — it is the standard digital-ad measurement spine that Google and Meta already use. The implication is that OpenAI is building ChatGPT ads as a real, salable inventory channel, not a cosmetic feature.

The move follows the September international rollout of ChatGPT ads in 31 European markets under GDPR, the August launch of ChatGPT ads in international shopping flows, and the $1 billion annualized ad run rate OpenAI reported in September. Taken together, the sequence is a steady operationalization of ads as a revenue line alongside subscriptions and enterprise. The strategic question is whether image-generation sessions — where the user is actively producing creative output — tolerate advertising at the same rate as search-style text sessions.

A takeaway for learners: the economics of generative AI are being rewritten in public. Inference is still priced below cost for free users, subscription growth has slowed in the mature cohorts, and advertising is the obvious third revenue line. Watch which product surfaces the ads land on first — image generation, then almost certainly voice and video — because those decisions will shape what 'using an AI assistant' feels like for the billion-plus users who never pay a subscription.
